summary.headline: Precision Camshafts Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 6.6% QoQ to INR173 crore and PAT to INR14.88 crore, while EMOSS Europe revenue fell to INR13.8 crore from INR29 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported standalone total income of INR173 crore (up 6.6% QoQ), with EBITDA margin of about 13% and PAT margin of about 9%, citing new program starts with Mahindra, Tata Motors and Maruti Suzuki. Consolidated revenue declined 2.4% QoQ to INR200.8 crore with EBITDA margin about 10%. The European EV subsidiary EMOSS weakened sharply and management is cautious on its outlook, while the Indian standalone business is framed as the growth engine. Management said results were achieved despite disruption from the Middle East war.

segments.name: Standalone India (PCL)
segments.commentary: Total income INR173 crore, up 6.6% QoQ; EBITDA margin about 13%, PAT margin about 9%. New programs with Mahindra, Tata Motors and Maruti Suzuki entered production in the quarter.

segments.name: MEMCO (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR14.1 crore in Q1; management is focusing on key customers Bosch, Delphi and Endress+Hauser.

segments.name: EMOSS (Netherlands, e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell to INR13.8 crore from INR29 crore QoQ; management is taking a cautious view and prioritising cost and investment protection.

segments.name: Own EHCV platform (India e-mobility)
segments.commentary: Electric heavy commercial vehicle platform developed; one vehicle delivered to a customer, now in evaluation and field trials. No revenue figure disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volumes from newly started programs to ramp progressively as customer production increases.
Several further new programs expected to commence production in coming quarters.
Continued investment in capacity, automation and technology in India, ahead of customer requirements.
Cautious near-term outlook for EMOSS Europe; will evaluate based on customer traction, cash needs and potential returns.
Cumulative order book of about INR1,500 crore over and above existing business, to be executed over four to five years (not annualised).
capex_capacity: Investing ahead of customer requirements in capacity additions, automation and technology upgrades in India; no specific capex amount or commissioning date given.
Management will remain disciplined on capital allocation and not pursue growth for its own sake.
Actively evaluating acquisition opportunities within India to add new products, markets and customers.
demand_pricing: Management describes Indian PV market growth as strong, with customers significantly investing in capacity, new vehicle programs and localisation.
Europe: electrically chargeable trucks were 4.8% of new EU truck registrations in H1 2026; EV commercial vehicle adoption constrained by weak enabling conditions and subsidy pullback.
European OEMs restructuring; EV customer decision-making slower and program visibility reduced.
No pricing or realisation data disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company focus only on camshafts or on other segments as well?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on the Indian standalone business and subsidiary MEMCO, which is developing several new products. Management is also actively looking at acquisitions within India to enter new products, markets and customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outstanding order book size?
qa_highlights.answer: A cumulative order book of about INR1,500 crore above existing business from existing and new customers was disclosed in earlier calls and the AGM. It is not annualised and will be spread over four to five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is EMOSS likely to be wound up, as the earlier Europe subsidiary was?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to say given rapidly changing markets. Management is trying to make EMOSS sustainable as a standalone business without support from India, and acknowledges significant headwinds.

risks_watch: EMOSS revenue fell about 52% QoQ to INR13.8 crore; possibility of further restructuring or winding up of the European subsidiary.
Slower EV commercial vehicle adoption in Europe and reduced program visibility.
Ramp pace of newly started programs with Mahindra, Tata Motors and Maruti Suzuki.
Execution of the INR1,500 crore order book over four to five years and the new pipeline.
Disruption from the Middle East war cited as a headwind; no quantification given.
Possible acquisitions in India, with no details on size or timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Indian standalone business and its program pipeline; cautious and somewhat non-committal on EMOSS, where management repeatedly said it is too early to predict the outcome. Management gave few specifics on order-book timing, capex amounts or EMOSS losses.
